title: The Second Harbor
premise: Astrid Lockridge built her wedding-planning empire on the ruins of her own broken engagement, and she trusts no one—least of all Elias Vane, the harbor-town lawyer whose negligence case nearly bankrupted her years ago. When a charity pen-pal program mismatches them as anonymous correspondents, their letters become the only honest space either has left, even as they unknowingly fall for the person they claim to hate. When their identities surface mid-scandal, with Astrid's company under federal investigation and Elias forced to choose between exposing her to save his career or protecting her and losing everything, the two must decide whether love is worth the price of survival. They choose each other, testify together to bring down the real culprit, and rebuild—Astrid planning one final wedding: her own, on the second harbor she once swore never to return to.
about_author: Wren Iversen is a former event coordinator who spent a decade behind the scenes of other people's happiest days before turning to fiction. She writes from a coastal cottage, where she insists the tide sets her writing schedule.

chapters.title: Mismatched Envelopes
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Astrid orchestrates a flawless society wedding while privately despising everything it represents, then grudgingly joins a harbor-town charity pen-pal program to salvage her company's image. The coordinator's clerical error pairs her with an anonymous correspondent she'll later learn is Elias Vane. Beat: guarded cynicism masking loneliness.

chapters.title: The Man Who Sank Her
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias, a rising attorney haunted by the malpractice suit that ruined Astrid's first business, receives his pen-pal assignment and begins writing with disarming honesty he shows no one else. A chance encounter with Astrid at the courthouse rekindles their open hostility. Beat: guilt sharpened into rivalry.

chapters.title: Letters to a Stranger
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Their letters deepen—Astrid confesses her lost engagement; Elias admits his career is built on a single catastrophic mistake. In person, they clash over a charity gala they're both forced to plan. Beat: intimacy growing in one place while animosity hardens in the other.

chapters.title: Salt and Paper
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Astrid realizes she's falling for her anonymous correspondent and begins comparing every man she meets to him, while Elias's charm at gala planning meetings starts to crack her contempt. A near-miss almost reveals their identities. Beat: longing she refuses to name.

chapters.title: The Subpoena
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias discovers his firm is investigating Astrid's company for fraud—and that his senior partner expects him to build the case using information from his pen-pal, whose identity he now suspects. He hides the conflict, lying to both sides. Beat: duty tightening like a noose.

chapters.title: What the Tide Brought In
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Federal investigators raid Astrid's office during a wedding; her career and reputation begin collapsing in public. Elias quietly shields her from a reporter, and for one evening their hostility dissolves into something tender and terrifying. Beat: ruin and unexpected grace.

chapters.title: Two Names, One Handwriting
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At the gala, a spilled envelope reveals the truth: her beloved correspondent is Elias Vane. Astrid feels betrayed twice over—by the deception and by the discovery that he may have known about the investigation. Beat: the cruelest revelation at the worst moment.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. His partner offers Elias partnership if he delivers Astrid's incriminating files; refusal ends his career. Elias instead finds evidence that the fraud was orchestrated by his own firm to bury an old liability—the same error that ruined Astrid years ago. Beat: the choice between survival and conscience.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Climax. Astrid, armed with Elias's evidence, chooses to testify rather than take a quiet settlement that would save her company but bury the truth. Elias betrays his firm on the stand beside her, ending his career as hers hangs by a thread. Beat: love proven through sacrifice, justice seized outside the system.

chapters.title: The Second Harbor
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Months later, exonerated and starting over with a small honest studio, Astrid plans one last wedding—her own, on the harbor she once fled. Elias arrives with the final letter, read aloud at the altar. Beat: hard-won peace; second chances, finally, at the right time.
